title: OOP & C++ Flashcards
subject: cpp-oop
description: Flashcards for OOP and C++ covering classes, inheritance, polymorphism, and STL for C-CAT preparation. Essential revision material for C-CAT aspirants.

cards.front: What are the four pillars of OOP?
Default access specifier in a C++ class
cards.back: private (a struct defaults to public instead)

cards.front: What does a pure virtual function look like, and what does it do?
cards.back: virtual void f() = 0; — makes the class abstract, uninstantiable

cards.front: Why must a base class destructor be virtual?
cards.back: So deleting a derived object via a base pointer also runs the derived destructor — otherwise cleanup is skipped
Base class constructor runs first, then the derived class constructor
Reverse of construction — derived class destructor first, then base

cards.front: What does the 'this' pointer refer to?
cards.back: A pointer to the calling object, implicitly passed to every non-static member function

cards.front: How many copies of a static data member exist across all objects of a class?
cards.back: Just 1 — shared by the entire class, not per-object

cards.front: What problem does virtual inheritance solve?
cards.back: The diamond problem — duplicate copies of a shared base class

cards.front: Difference between function overloading and overriding
cards.back: Overloading = same name, different parameters, resolved at compile-time. Overriding = same signature in a derived class, resolved at runtime, needs virtual

cards.front: Which operators cannot be overloaded in C++?
What must new[] be paired with?
cards.back: delete[] — mismatching it with a plain delete causes undefined behavior
A non-member function explicitly granted access to a class's private and protected members

cards.front: Which STL container keeps its elements in sorted order automatically?
cards.back: std::map — implemented as a self-balancing tree (typically Red-Black)
